why: Each entry records one published package's OPEN correction round: the issue that owns the round, the clock that round is measured against, the package it governs, and the claim sites it requires changed. `stepgate.py` reads this file off the tree and counts a disagreement at one of those sites as OWNED while the round is open and its clock has not passed; it exits non-zero only on the disagreements no round owns. Two expiries, both mechanical: an entry recorded `closed` owns nothing, and an entry whose clock has passed owns nothing - an entry that cannot expire is an allowlist wearing a number. The reader is the cycle opener (README.md, submission workflow step 0): re-read every entry against the issue it names, and retire it when the round ends. A listed site that occupies no finding is printed by the gate as a note, so a discharged round is visible rather than silently stale.

rounds.note: Correction round 2 was OPENED R629 at 573dd41 and CLOSED at dac89f9, the squash merge of PR #152 (verified at c7ae675 in comment 6402211633): the two manuscript lines now state the pair the script takes, so the sites this entry named occupy no finding - the gate prints them as a note, which is what a discharged round looks like. Retired by recording it closed rather than by deleting it: the round is a fact of the record, and both expiries stay mechanical - a closed entry owns nothing, so if these lines ever disagree again the finding comes back UNOWNED and the gate exits 1.
